headline_seed: Marseille braces for more unrest after protests give way to 'apocalyptic' disorder - BBC

consensus_facts: Both BBC full-text articles (Articles 2 and 4) are identical in content and report the same event: Marseille experienced severe disorder on Saturday as protests escalated into looting and vandalism.
Marseille authorities banned public gatherings for an eight-hour window (reported by the BBC bodies and corroborated at headline level by The Times of Israel's 'noon to 8 p.m.' framing).

framing_analysis.Associated Press (wire): Headline-only in this dossier. Frames the story through the commercial/sports angle — soccer clubs Marseille and Lille closing shops after vandalism and looting. Emphasizes economic impact rather than politics or policing. No body text available to assess further.
framing_analysis.BBC News (international): Provides the only substantive full-text reporting (Articles 2 and 4 are duplicates; Article 3 is a stub). Leads with atmospheric 'apocalyptic' disorder framing and the scale of damage: 500+ premises damaged, majority looted, 118 officers injured (over a tenth of the national figure), 101 arrests (a quarter of them children). Centers the police-union perspective (Arnaud Blaise, UN1TE) attributing provocation to far-left 'Black Bloc' agitators and looting to youths from deprived northern suburbs. Balances this by putting the heavy-handedness accusation directly to the union and quoting Socialist Mayor Benoît Payan calling the response a 'fiasco.' Includes voices of a young protester (Maryame) weighing the legitimacy of violence and a 79-year-old resident. Notes Interior Minister Nuñez's rejected resignation and Macron's refusal to accept it, plus curfews for minors in Marseille and Paris.
framing_analysis.The Times of Israel: Headline-only in this dossier. Frames narrowly on the public-order measure — the ban on all gatherings from noon to 8 p.m. after violent protests. Emphasizes the state response/restriction angle. No body text available to assess further.

primary_source_alignment: No primary sources were located for this story. No court filings, press releases, official statements, or transcripts were available to verify claims against.
missing_context: EDITORIAL DISCLOSURE — SINGLE-SOURCE LIMITATION: Only one outlet (BBC) provided substantive body text, and Articles 2 and 4 are the same BBC piece duplicated. AP and The Times of Israel appear headline-only. Therefore nearly all specific details (500+ premises damaged, 118 officers injured, 101 arrests, 4,000 tear gas grenades, curfew timings, Nuñez's rejected resignation) are single-source BBC reporting, NOT corroborated wire consensus.

The specific figures for property damage, injuries, and arrests are attributed within the BBC piece to local business leaders and a police union — not independently verified by multiple outlets in this dossier.
No outlet in the dossier provides data on injuries to protesters or civilians, only police injuries — the BBC notes the heavy-handedness accusation but does not quantify the other side.

The underlying cause and timeline of the protest movement is only briefly sketched (began in September over poor school conditions, broadened to cost of living); no outlet provides deeper background on the movement's organizers or national scope.
No independent verification of the 'Black Bloc' / far-left attribution, which comes solely from the police union within the BBC article; the claim is contested framing, not established fact.
No outlet reports the national totals (total nationwide injuries, arrests, or affected cities) beyond the BBC noting Marseille's 118 injuries were 'more than a tenth of the national figure.'
brief.suggested_post_type_reason: Only one outlet (BBC) supplied substantive body text — with its two full-text articles being duplicates — while AP and The Times of Israel are headline-only, so there is no genuine multi-source consensus to anchor a REPORT. The story is time-sensitive and ongoing, warranting a same-day, single-source-hedged bulletin that flags the BBC-dependent sourcing.
